not_to_be_confused_with: world/items/<id>_interface.json, where one exists, is the MODULE's own published contract -- datums, sockets, constants. This file is the CAMPAIGN's ownership decision about the same item and does not replace it.
why: WAVE2-SCOPE 3.3. This item is a FLOOR: the world already builds the surface at class level and the item's value to a dependant is the datum, not a silhouette. The class keeps the geometry; this file is what the module would otherwise have shipped.
read_this_instead: world_contract.world_ground_z(x, y) -- the analytic field. TER_Ground is the MESH of that field and every class builder already reads the field, not the mesh. A dependant must do the same: the mesh is cut away inside the road corridor and the platform, so a ray-cast against it returns nothing exactly where most items stand.

measured_overlap_with_the_module.note: A containment fraction is an UPPER bound -- a bed's bounding box swallows whatever stands on it. The control is printed beside it for that reason: where the control reads high, the subject's high reading means less.

argument: The clearest CLASS verdict in the set, and the one that most needed measuring rather than reading. TER_Ground is a single 638,365-vertex graded grid running x -10,907 to +10,827 and y -10,487 to +11,217 -- 21.7 km square. It is the film's horizon. The item is a ten-object hero patch of the same material. Superseding a horizon with a patch is the hole this exercise exists to prevent, and it would strand 24,646 trees, 2.98 M grass clumps and 1.62 M grit pieces on air. This is also WAVE2-SCOPE 3.3's case exactly -- geometry that exists so other items can read its z -- so the class keeps the geometry and the item becomes an interface stub.
